issues: The definition in the notes is wrong for the later editions. 'Covers most of the private sector (and usually the public sector)' is the 2011 test ('laws that at least cover most of their private sector'). The 2017 abstract counts 'comprehensive data privacy laws for the private sector, public sector, or (in most cases) both', and the 2019 abstract says 'covering both the private sector and public sectors in most cases'. From at least 2017, then, a law that covers only the public sector can count. The pre-2011 running sums, which use the 2011 test, are therefore not strictly comparable with the 2015+ points. The notes are corrected.

The 2011 point note ('Greenleaf's own table revised this to 81 by 10 November 2011 after re-applying his criteria') is not supported by any cited source. The SSRN abstract of paper 1946700 has no '81' and no 'November'. Removed.

The 2025 source's citation '(2025) 194 PLBIR' and its institution 'Privacy Laws & Business International Report' are not on the cited page. The SSRN capture gives only 'Greenleaf, Graham, 172 Countries with Data Privacy Laws -Year by Year 1973-2025 (March 23, 2025). Available at SSRN', with 3 pages, posted 28 Apr 2025. PL&B's site and Macquarie's research portal could not be reached to confirm an issue number, so the unverified journal citation is removed from the title and institution (series source 0 and points[1], points[14]).

'Published in Privacy Laws & Business International Report since 2011' overstates it slightly. The 2013 edition (99 countries) was published in the Journal of Law, Information & Science 23(1). The notes now say 'mostly'.

Checked and correct: every value (0, 1, 7, 17, 36, 68, 76, 99, 109, 120, 132, 145, 157, 162, 172) matches its quoted abstract, and the running sums 7+10+19+32 = 68 and +8 = 76 are right. Sweden 1973 is the first national law and Hesse 1970 the first law overall. The rates 3.3 a year and 5.4 a year since 2020 are verbatim. The dates and PL&B issue/page citations of the 2011, 2015, 2017, 2019, 2021, 2022 and 2023 editions match SSRN's suggested citations (e.g. '(2023) 181 Privacy Laws and Business International Report (PLBIR) 1, 2-4, UNSW Law Research Paper No. 23-48'). The 2015 abstract independently confirms the mid-2013 count of 99 ('since the last assessment in mid-2013 listing 99 countries').

fieldFixes.notes: Graham Greenleaf's roughly biennial global count, published mostly in Privacy Laws & Business International Report since 2011 (the 2013 edition appeared in the Journal of Law, Information & Science). A 'data privacy law' must meet minimum formal standards drawn from the OECD Guidelines and Council of Europe Convention 108. His 2011 count also required it to cover most of the private sector. From at least the 2017 edition he counts laws covering the private sector, the public sector or (in most cases) both, so the pre-2011 points (running sums of his 2011 decade counts) use a slightly narrower test than the later editions. Separate legal jurisdictions (e.g. Faroe Islands) count as 'countries'. His 2025 year-by-year list (SSRN 5189972, 3 pages) could not be retrieved, so points between editions are not interpolated. Counts are as at the date of each edition, not year-end. Average growth 1973-2025: 3.3 new countries a year; since 2020: 5.4 a year.
fieldFixes.points[6].note: As of mid-2011 (Greenleaf's first global count).
